parts.label: a
parts.ask: A balloon is modelled as a sphere whose radius \(r\) cm increases at a rate inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{r}\). Write down a differential equation for this.
parts.method: Turn the words into an equation

steps.text: Rate of increase of \(r\): \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{r}\): a constant over \(\sqrt{r}\).

check.answers: a model written from words: no number to compare

parts.label: b
parts.ask: At \(t = 10\) the radius is 16 cm and is increasing at 0.9 cm s⁻¹. Solve the differential equation to show that \(r^{\frac{3}{2}} = 5.4t + 10\).

steps.why: Add 1 to the power, divide by the new power \(\tfrac{3}{2}\).

parts.label: c
parts.ask: Hence find the radius when \(t = 20\), to the nearest millimetre.

steps.why: Power \(\tfrac{2}{3}\) undoes \(\tfrac{3}{2}\). Nearest mm is 1 d.p. in cm.

parts.label: d
parts.ask: Suggest a limitation of the model.

steps.text: In the model \(r^{\frac{3}{2}} = 5.4t + 10\), \(r\) grows for ever.

parts.answerText: A real balloon will burst, so the model cannot hold for large \(t\). (A balloon is also not a perfect sphere.)

check.answers: a comment on the model: no number to compare
